newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Clinton aide Kantor-dlr fall vs yen helps trade.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Clinton aide Kantor-dlr fall vs yen helps trade.

text.p: Former Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor said Monday the dollar's recent decline in foreign exchange trading will reduce the U.S.-Japan trade deficit, adding that the dollar had been "unusually high."
"It will be helpful for our trade balance. The dollar was unusually high and unusually high for a long time," Kantor told reporters after a speech to an auto dealers' convention.
Kantor cited higher Japanese market interest rates for the dollar's drop to under 116 yen from a recent peak near 127.50 and characterized the decline as a "good" thing.

"Now we have a very strong economy, that was part of it. But part of the reason it started to go down is because Japan is raising interest rates, which means they'll attract more capital, which is good for Japan. But it's also good in terms of lowering the cost of a dollar, the dollar/yen ratio, which is good for the U.S. economy," he added.
